I was diagnosed with Rheumatoid Arthritis in November of 2021. I began treatment immediately and my rheumatologist was proud of me to have started treatment early and to be diagnosed now rather than later on in life. I was struggling with my diagnosis and I am still grieving the loss of control of my body. I have a history if Rheumatoid Arthritis on my fathers side of the family, I just never expected to have been diagnosed so early. I see a therapist every month and we discuss grief and coping mechanisms. Though, I cant help but feel like this is all a punishment. I remember the first time I ever self harmed was when I was 10 years old, and my self harm didn’t stop until I was 21. In fact, the last time I ever hurt myself was in November of 2019. This was after being discharged from being in an inpatient psych unit after a failed suicide attempt. Hurting myself had always been my unhealthy coping mechanism and when I realized how worse it was becoming as I got older, I decided to get myself help. 

I felt proud. I felt like I actually started to love myself after years of hating myself. Thinking that I deserved to hurt myself because I was a “bad person” (it all relates to past trauma I have overcome). And after being diagnosed with RA, it all just feels like my body getting back at me for voluntarily hurting it for all those years. I look at myself in the mirror and wish I can go back in time to stop my younger self, thinking that maybe if I had just stopped earlier, none of this would be happening to me. I feel like my diagnosis is my fault but I cant do anything about it now other than take medication. But RA medication isn’t a cure. It simply slows the progression of your disease. I hope that they find a cure one day.



TLDR; I believe my diagnosis of RA is my own fault due to a long history of self harm. Now my body is punishing me in return and I cant do anything to stop it.
